source.title: Double Trouble in Double Descent : Bias and Variance(s) in the Lazy Regime
source.authors: Stéphane d'Ascoli; Maria Refinetti; G. Biroli; Florent Krzakala

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies the double-descent claim using random-feature regression and lazy-regime neural-network experiments, with bias/variance decomposition and ensembling as its methods.
record.gate_note: Own results bear on double descent and the effect of ensembling. Cited results from other work are not rows. The primary random-feature results use synthetic Gaussian data and a linear teacher; the neural-network experiment uses a binary task derived from CIFAR-10. Figure-only values are not numerically reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures how held-out error changes beyond interpolation as width increases, bearing on V2 through random-feature theory and five-layer network experiments. Different architectures, data and training methods do not make that width-generalization question untested.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate when restricted to the RF model and qualitative lazy-learning comparison. Noise and initialization variances cause the interpolation peak and post-interpolation decline; bias and sampling variance plateau at vanishing regularization. Ensembling suppresses those variances, producing a post-interpolation plateau in the infinite-ensemble limit. The finite neural-network ensemble is roughly flat near lazy learning and rises beyond interpolation farther from that regime.
record.recipe_differences: Analytical random-feature regression and a numerical lazy-regime neural-network experiment, rather than the listed original studies' interventions. Gaussian inputs and a linear teacher in the analytical model; binary 10-PCA CIFAR-10 for the neural-network experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Ensemble size K; regularization λ; signal-to-noise ratio; dataset size N/D; proximity to lazy regime controlled by α. The paper reports that the neural-network curve differs between α = 100 and α = 10.

fits_no_version.finding: Ensembling suppresses the interpolation peak by reducing initialization and noise variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Averaging independently initialized lazy predictors suppresses the interpolation peak.

fits_no_version.finding: Doubling features and averaging two predictors offer different improvements as dataset size varies.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relative benefit of ensembling and increasing features depends on dataset size and feature dimension.

fits_no_version.finding: The infinite RF ensemble outperforms the optimally regularized single predictor in the tested comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization averaging can improve RF regression beyond tuning a single predictor's ridge penalty.

fits_no_version.finding: More averaging, lower SNR or smaller datasets can move the global error minimum below interpolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The globally optimal RF model size can be underparametrized even when post-interpolation error decreases.

record.problems: The analytic results use a heuristic, non-rigorous replica method. The main model uses synthetic i.i.d. Gaussian data and a linear teacher. The realistic neural-network experiment is a binary task on only the first ten PCA components of CIFAR-10; the paper describes it as qualitative. Finite-size simulation variability is reported for some figures.
record.rows_left_out: No separately stated numerical result rows were omitted. Several curve comparisons are described qualitatively in the text and figures without exact values; those are recorded as stated rather than reconstructed.

untested.parts: No fixed-random-label fitting experiment or matched comparison with natural-label generalization.

The original one-hidden-layer, fully trained ReLU classification recipe on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10 without explicit regularization is not reproduced. RF regression fixes the first layer and uses ridge regularization; the image experiment uses five-layer networks and binary PCA-reduced CIFAR-10.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No optimizer comparison or tuning-budget intervention.
No comparison of batch sizes or epoch budgets.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking of generalization measures.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining comparison.

missing.what: Record the infinite-ensemble post-interpolation plateau separately from interpolation-peak suppression. The text explicitly states that test error remains constant beyond interpolation when K tends to infinity.
missing.locator: Abstract; Section 5, equations 24–27 and discussion accompanying Figures 5–6.

missing.what: Separate the K = 1 width curves from the K = 20 ensemble curves in the neural-network experiment. Figure 9 reports both, but R6–R7 record only ensemble outcomes; single-predictor post-interpolation trends are needed for the closest comparison with V2.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source of V2. Ensemble results qualify extensions of the width claim; they do not refute the original single-network experiment. A global optimum below interpolation and a peak at interpolation are distinct from V2's continuing post-interpolation decrease.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fit random labels or compare natural-label and random-label generalization.
The study does not test widening one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10 as described.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
The neural-network experiment uses Adam alone and does not compare adaptive and SGD optimizers.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No memorized-example removal and retraining experiment.

rows.subject: Random Feature (RF) model
rows.size_stated: High-dimensional limit: N, P, D go to infinity with ratios fixed; finite-size numerical estimation D = 200
rows.operation_detail: Varied overparametrization ratio P/N and decomposed test error into noise, initialization, sampling and bias components.
rows.measure: Mean-square test error and its bias/variance decomposition
rows.value: At the interpolation threshold P = N, noise and initialization variances diverge at vanishing regularization; sampling variance and bias remain finite, show a kink, then plateau. For P > N, test-error decrease is due to noise and initialization variances decreasing.
rows.note: This is a random-feature regression model on Gaussian inputs with a linear ground truth and noisy labels; the measured error decomposition does not match a listed version.
rows.check: The stated post-interpolation decrease directly bears on V2. This is ReLU random-feature regression with fixed first-layer weights and small ridge regularization, rather than fully trained classification networks. D = 200 describes numerical checks, not the analytical limit.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4, Interpolation Threshold and Overparametrized regime; Figure 3 caption.

rows.subject: Random Feature (RF) model
rows.size_stated: High-dimensional limit: N, P, D go to infinity with ratios fixed; finite-size numerical estimation D = 200
rows.operation_detail: Varied ensemble size K while measuring test error as a function of P/N.
rows.value: As K increases, the overfitting peak at the interpolation threshold is diminished; for K → ∞, the divergence at P = N is entirely suppressed.
rows.uncertainty: For finite D = 200, vertical bars depict standard deviation over 10 runs.
rows.note: Ensembling independently initialized RF models trained on the same dataset.
rows.check: Peak suppression alone does not establish V2's post-interpolation width trend. The caption's reference to N tending to infinity appears to be a typo for ensemble size K tending to infinity; equations and surrounding discussion identify K as the relevant limit.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5, equation (23), Figures 5–6 and Ensembling reduces the double trouble.

rows.subject: Random Feature (RF) model
rows.size_stated: High-dimensional limit: N, P, D go to infinity with ratios fixed
rows.operation_detail: Compared test-error curves for vanilla, ensembled and divide-and-conquer predictors as P/N varied.
rows.value: Doubling features and ensembling over two initializations have different effects; overparametrization shifts the interpolation threshold, and ensembling outperforms it in a region. The asymptotic improvement from overparametrization is higher in the large-dataset limit; the gap is reduced as P/D increases.
rows.note: The prose describes relative curve behavior without giving numerical values.
rows.check: Figure 7 varies N/D at fixed P/D = 0.5 or 5, not P/N by widening at fixed dataset size. Its comparison of doubling features with ensembling does not by itself establish the post-interpolation width trend.

rows.subject: Random Feature (RF) model
rows.size_stated: High-dimensional limit: N, P, D go to infinity with ratios fixed
rows.operation_detail: Compared an infinitely ensembled predictor with the optimally regularized single predictor.

conditions.value: K = 1 optimized over 50 values of λ from 10−5 to 102; K → ∞ uses λ = 10−5

rows.value: An infinitely ensembled model always performs better than an optimally regularized single model.
rows.note: The stated comparison is for the paper's random-feature regression setup.
rows.check: This row records an ensemble-versus-regularization advantage, not the width effect named by V2. The stated comparison is supported within the tested RF setup; its original observed state describes that separate finding.

rows.subject: Random Feature (RF) model
rows.size_stated: High-dimensional limit: N, P, D go to infinity with ratios fixed
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of averaged predictors, signal-to-noise ratio, and dataset size relative to dimension while comparing test error across P/N.
rows.value: The minimum generalization error can move to the underparametrized regime as K increases, SNR decreases, or N/D decreases.
rows.note: No numerical values are stated in the text for the plotted curves.
rows.check: An underparametrized global optimum does not contradict decreasing error within the overparametrized regime. V2 does not assert that the global minimum must lie beyond interpolation.

rows.subject: 5-layer fully-connected network
rows.size_stated: Number of nodes per layer varied; interpolation occurs around 30 nodes per layer
rows.operation_detail: Varied width and compared one predictor with an ensemble of 20 independently initialized networks.

conditions.value: binary 10-PCA CIFAR-10; classes grouped by parity of labels

rows.value: For α = 100, the K = 20 test-error curve becomes roughly flat beyond the interpolation threshold, around 30 nodes per layer.
rows.uncertainty: For K = 1, standard deviation is depicted as vertical bars, averaged over 20 initializations.
rows.note: The stated outcome is for the ensemble in the setting closer to the lazy regime.
rows.check: The ensemble's roughly flat post-interpolation curve shows no continuing width benefit in this condition. The relevant comparison is across widths within K = 20, rather than K = 20 against K = 1. Training lasted 10^5 steps.
